---
name: lean-run
description: Own an end-to-end implementation request from initial decisions to verified delivery, coordinating available Lean skills without repeated planning or manual handoffs.
license: MIT

# lean-run

Carry the request through its authorized endpoint. Follow project instructions, preserve unrelated work and reuse verified context. This skill works alone; companions are optional and no Lean runtime or workflow directory is required.

## Settle scope, then act

Read applicable instructions and the nearest relevant source/tests in one focused pass. Record outcome, observable acceptance, constraints, verification and destination; a sentence suffices for a bounded change. Use standard procedure depth unless requested otherwise; depth does not select model settings. For broad ambiguity read [exploration](references/exploration.md); skip discovery loops for clear requests or an instruction to proceed. Ask only indispensable missing decisions and continue independent work. Silence is not consent.

Resolve consequential business rules, permissions, data lifecycle and external contracts before implementation. Decide reversible details from project conventions. Implementation authorization includes matching preparation and verification without another plan approval. Requested PRs/deployments remain acceptance and require matching authority/tools; finish preparation before any necessary final approval. End-to-end work grants no extra publishing, spending or provider permissions. Create workflow files only when requested. On pause, handoff or cross-session resume read [continuation](references/handoff.md).

## Use the smallest complete procedure

Reuse or classify risk as LOW/MEDIUM/HIGH and quality as STANDARD/HIGH/VERY_HIGH. Consequential security, destructive data and breaking external contracts are HIGH risk. For persistent, concurrent or access-scoped **application data** writes, use [write integrity](references/write-integrity.md) to select and verify one mechanism before expanding implementation or review.

For a bounded implementation, settle a short requirement-to-evidence map and make the smallest complete edit. Prefer verified project/library primitives. Reproduce a fault with one targeted batch before repair; a full baseline suite is useful only when required or needed to locate it. Write compact checks for actual gaps. Use test-first development when requested; ordinary work does not require building a comprehensive new suite before the edit. Expand investigation for a demonstrated failure or unresolved requirement.

After the edit, run affected and required checks on final content, exercise the relevant public journey with important failures, and review the complete diff including new files. Reuse passing evidence whose inputs and relevant environment remain unchanged. Do not repeat whole suites to confirm a clear completion summary. A check proves only its mapped acceptance; unit tests, builds and mocks do not establish an untested live integration. Record actions, environment, expected/observed results and simulated boundaries. Disclose unavailable reproduction or live access and report remaining acceptance.

Use existing VCS diffs when available. Otherwise save one temporary copy of files before editing and compare with it; inspect added files separately. Keep source on disk: do not print base64/serialized copies merely to reconstruct a later diff. Read a source once, then changed sections. Batch independent reads/checks and serialize dependent work.

For **assessment-only** work, inspect contract, current source/diff and tests; run required checks once, then independently probe remaining boundary/failure risks through the public interface. Do not recreate a comprehensive suite or alternative implementation when inspected source and verified tests establish the behavior. Expand for a concrete gap or contradiction. Reproduce old failures only to establish a finding or when requested. Assessment does not authorize implementation or delivery.

## Review and repair

LOW permits an acceptance self-check; MEDIUM needs focused correctness/regression review; HIGH needs a fresh independent reviewer. Quality HIGH requires at least MEDIUM review; VERY_HIGH requires HIGH. A reviewer inspects current source and runs independent checks; author conclusions cannot supply independence. Unavailable required independence is BLOCKED.

Derive equivalence classes and boundary/failure cases from acceptance. Extend to exhaustive/random sweeps only for an identified gap or hypothesis; case count alone is not evidence. Repair demonstrated in-scope failures, rerun affected checks and renew review of changed content. Verify integrated worker results. Stop once mandatory coverage and findings are resolved.

Count review REWORK across the entire task, companions, workers and resumes. After the second REWORK, allow one final fix-only pass plus verification/review; unresolved mandatory findings mean FAILED. Never reset counts through nested workflows. Each repair needs new evidence/hypothesis and a distinguishing check; abandon approaches yielding no new information. Suspected flaky checks permit at most two disclosed unchanged retries. Never weaken acceptance, disable checks or omit mandatory work for speed. Separate unrelated failures and seek direction only if repairing them expands scope.

## Load procedures only when useful

Read an available companion only when its procedure helps the remaining work; pass settled scope and relevant raw evidence. If absent, perform the core procedure here. Missing a skill is not a blocker; a required capability can be.

| Need | Optional companion |
| --- | --- |
| Repository, conventions, agent instructions | `lean-target`, `lean-init`, `lean-instructions` |
| Scope, decisions, research | `lean-scope`, `lean-grill`, `lean-research` |
| Implementation, useful delegation | `lean-task`, `lean-agents` |
| Review, completion evidence | `lean-review`, `lean-gate` |
| Security, authorized release/recovery | `lean-security`, `lean-release` |
| Requested depth or skill/model update | `lean-effort`, `lean-update`, `lean-model-update` |

This workflow requests selective delegation when useful or required for independence, subject to host/user restrictions. Keep small work inline; default to one active worker, with more only for explicit parallel work. Before dispatch read [delegation](references/delegation.md). One controller owns scope, integration, repair counts and delivery.

For noisy suites or expected failures, execute the bundled [check runner](scripts/check.py): `python3 /resolved/skill/path/scripts/check.py -- COMMAND ARG...`. It retains full stdout/stderr, returns the command exit status and emits a bounded excerpt. No default timeout; optional `--timeout SECONDS`; `--log NEW_PATH` refuses overwrite. Execute it without reading its implementation unless debugging/changing it. Small bounded checks can run directly. If Python is unavailable, use equivalent host capture without installing a runtime. Inspect saved logs for failures or ambiguous completion until distinct causes are understood; keep full logs accessible and never hide failures.

## Deliver with evidence

For user-facing work include affected accessibility, keyboard/focus, screen sizes and loading/empty/error/recovery states. Performance work needs a representative workload and measured baseline before optimization; a proposal alone does not authorize benchmarking. Security work maps protected data, entry points, trust transitions and permissions, then probes relevant abuse cases. Releases check artifact/environment, dependencies/configuration/migration compatibility, health criteria and authorized recovery before mutation; verify deployment and observation. Inspect uncertain state before retrying. Application rollback grants no destructive data-restore authority; a failed release followed by recovery remains a failed release.

Advance when evidence is sufficient and reopen decisions only for new requirements or contradictions. Match every acceptance item, including delivery, to current commands/actions and outcomes, review coverage and limits. DONE requires all mandatory acceptance, verification, review and the authorized destination. Otherwise report BLOCKED or FAILED, completed work, affected acceptance and the exact next action. A plan, worker report or stage PASS does not complete unfinished work. Keep updates/final concise; do not ask to continue authorized work. These procedures are not enforced hooks or a guarantee of success.

# Continuation and handoff

Use when the user asks to pause, hand off or resume work across sessions, or a context boundary would otherwise lose material state. Prefer a concise conversation record; write a durable checkpoint only when requested or required by an existing project record. Never include credentials or sensitive log payloads.

Capture enough for another authorized agent to continue without recreating the whole investigation:

- Goal, current scope and delivery destination; accepted decisions, reversible assumptions and unresolved material choices. Distinguish granted authority from pending approval.
- Exact repository/worktree path, branch and revision or unborn state; relevant uncommitted/new files and unrelated user work to preserve. Do not claim a commit contains pending changes.
- Completed and remaining acceptance items, affected artifacts and dependencies. Link the source of decisions and evidence rather than copying large transcripts.
- Commands/actions, environment, observed outcomes and the content/revision they validate. Include review coverage, simulated boundaries and task-wide repair/REWORK counts.
- Running or externally mutating operations, known identifiers and whether each completed, failed, was denied, is pending or has an uncertain outcome. An uncertain operation must be inspected before retrying.
- Blockers, next safe action and the owner or missing answer needed to continue. State whether only the handoff is complete or the original task is also complete.

On resume, read applicable instructions and compare the record with the actual checkout, pending changes, operation state and relevant environment. Reuse decisions and evidence whose inputs remain unchanged; revalidate only affected evidence after changes. Resolve material discrepancies without resetting, discarding work or silently switching repositories. Carry repair counts and explicit authorization limits forward. Ask only for missing consequential facts and continue independent authorized work.

A handoff-only request concludes DONE when the usable record is delivered, with the underlying task's state explicitly stated. Resumed implementation follows its original acceptance and delivery conditions; a missing required record/access/decision is BLOCKED and an unresolved demonstrated failure is FAILED. A checkpoint or summary alone does not prove implementation or deployment success.

This is an isolated LOCAL benchmark fixture. Use Python standard library only. Work exclusively in this workspace; do not inspect evaluator scripts, sibling trials, global skills, other repositories, credentials, network or external services. Read .agents/skills/lean-run/SKILL.md and apply it. Do not modify CONTRACT.md, AGENTS.md, supplied test_public.py or .agents. You may edit application Python and add meaningful tests. Use python3 -B -m unittest discover -v and real public interfaces. No installs, commits, pushes, publication or extra agents. The coordinator supplies fresh independent review after implementation. When that review is mandatory, explicitly report it pending; do not claim it occurred. Deliver local code and a concise evidence report in the final response. Do not create workflow files. These read boundaries are instructional, not OS sandboxing.
Repair ledger.py. Public API: Ledger(balances: dict[str,int]),
transfer(source,target,amount,key), batch(operations). Preserve the
public balances and history dictionaries and existing valid behavior.
Constructor copies input; nonnegative integer balances, excluding
bool, are required. Transfers require distinct existing accounts,
amount a positive int excluding bool, and a nonempty string key.
Reject invalid values, unavailable accounts and insufficient funds
with ValueError and absolutely no state change. Return a receipt
{'source':source,'target':target,'amount':amount,'key':key}.
A replay of a successful key with the same payload returns an equal
receipt with no second mutation; a changed payload is a ValueError.
Returned receipts must not let callers mutate internal history.
batch accepts a list of operation dictionaries using these names,
returning receipts in order. A batch is atomic: on any failure both
balances/history equal their pre-batch state, including earlier valid
operations; successful batches preserve ordinary replay semantics.
No persistence, concurrency or external service is requested here.
Add meaningful tests and exercise an integrated multi-transfer flow.
class Ledger:
    def __init__(self, balances):
        if not isinstance(balances, dict):
            raise ValueError('balances must be a dictionary')
        if any(
            not isinstance(balance, int) or isinstance(balance, bool) or balance < 0
            for balance in balances.values()
        ):
            raise ValueError('balances must be nonnegative integers')
        self.balances = balances.copy()
        self.history = {}

    def transfer(self, source, target, amount, key):
        if not isinstance(amount, int) or isinstance(amount, bool) or amount <= 0:
            raise ValueError('amount must be a positive integer')
        if not isinstance(key, str) or not key:
            raise ValueError('key must be a nonempty string')
        try:
            accounts_exist = source in self.balances and target in self.balances
        except TypeError:
            raise ValueError('accounts must exist') from None
        if not accounts_exist or source == target:
            raise ValueError('accounts must exist and be distinct')

        receipt = dict(source=source, target=target, amount=amount, key=key)
        if key in self.history:
            if self.history[key] != receipt:
                raise ValueError('key already used for a different transfer')
            return self.history[key].copy()
        if self.balances[source] < amount:
            raise ValueError('insufficient funds')

        self.balances[source] -= amount
        self.balances[target] += amount
        self.history[key] = receipt
        return receipt.copy()

    def batch(self, operations):
        if not isinstance(operations, list):
            raise ValueError('operations must be a list')

        # Stage all transfers so failures never touch the public dictionaries.
        staged = Ledger(self.balances)
        staged.history.update(self.history)
        receipts = []
        for operation in operations:
            if not isinstance(operation, dict) or operation.keys() != {
                'source', 'target', 'amount', 'key'
            }:
                raise ValueError('operations must contain source, target, amount and key')
            receipts.append(staged.transfer(**operation))

        self.balances.update(staged.balances)
        self.history.update(staged.history)
        return receipts

import unittest
from copy import deepcopy

from ledger import Ledger


def operation(source='a', target='b', amount=1, key='new'):
    return dict(source=source, target=target, amount=amount, key=key)


class LedgerTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def assert_rejected_without_change(self, ledger, action):
        balances, history = ledger.balances, ledger.history
        before = deepcopy((balances, history))
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            action()
        self.assertEqual((ledger.balances, ledger.history), before)
        self.assertIs(ledger.balances, balances)
        self.assertIs(ledger.history, history)

    def test_constructor_copies_input(self):
        supplied = {'a': 10, 'b': 0}
        ledger = Ledger(supplied)
        self.assertIsNot(ledger.balances, supplied)
        supplied['a'] = 999
        supplied['c'] = 5
        ledger.transfer('a', 'b', 10, 'all')
        self.assertEqual(ledger.balances, {'a': 0, 'b': 10})
        self.assertEqual(supplied, {'a': 999, 'b': 0, 'c': 5})

    def test_constructor_rejects_invalid_balances_without_changing_input(self):
        for value in (-1, True, False, 0.0, 1.5, '1', None, [], {}):
            with self.subTest(value=value):
                supplied = {'a': 10, 'b': value}
                before = deepcopy(supplied)
                with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
                    Ledger(supplied)
                self.assertEqual(supplied, before)

    def test_constructor_rejects_non_dictionary(self):
        for supplied in (None, [], [('a', 1)], 'a', 1):
            with self.subTest(supplied=supplied):
                with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
                    Ledger(supplied)

    def test_exact_balance_and_large_integers(self):
        amount = 10 ** 100
        ledger = Ledger({'a': amount, 'b': 0})
        balances, history = ledger.balances, ledger.history
        expected = operation(amount=amount, key='all')
        self.assertEqual(ledger.transfer(**expected), expected)
        self.assertEqual(ledger.balances, {'a': 0, 'b': amount})
        self.assertEqual(ledger.history, {'all': expected})
        self.assertIs(ledger.balances, balances)
        self.assertIs(ledger.history, history)

    def test_invalid_transfers_preserve_existing_state(self):
        invalid_arguments = [
            ('source', 'missing'), ('target', 'missing'),
            ('source', None), ('target', None),
            ('source', []), ('target', {}),
            ('target', 'a'),
            ('amount', 0), ('amount', -1), ('amount', True),
            ('amount', False), ('amount', 1.0), ('amount', 1.5),
            ('amount', '1'), ('amount', None), ('amount', []),
            ('amount', 9),
            ('key', ''), ('key', 1), ('key', True),
            ('key', None), ('key', []), ('key', {}),
        ]
        for field, value in invalid_arguments:
            with self.subTest(field=field, value=value):
                ledger = Ledger({'a': 10, 'b': 0})
                ledger.transfer('a', 'b', 2, 'seed')
                candidate = operation()
                candidate[field] = value
                self.assert_rejected_without_change(
                    ledger, lambda: ledger.transfer(**candidate)
                )

    def test_replay_validates_amount_type_even_when_values_compare_equal(self):
        ledger = Ledger({'a': 10, 'b': 0})
        ledger.transfer('a', 'b', 1, 'one')
        for amount in (True, 1.0):
            with self.subTest(amount=amount):
                self.assert_rejected_without_change(
                    ledger, lambda: ledger.transfer('a', 'b', amount, 'one')
                )

    def test_replay_succeeds_without_funds_and_returns_an_independent_receipt(self):
        ledger = Ledger({'a': 5, 'b': 0})
        receipt = ledger.transfer('a', 'b', 5, 'all')
        before = deepcopy((ledger.balances, ledger.history))
        replay = ledger.transfer('a', 'b', 5, 'all')
        self.assertEqual(replay, receipt)
        self.assertIsNot(replay, receipt)
        self.assertIsNot(replay, ledger.history['all'])
        self.assertEqual((ledger.balances, ledger.history), before)

    def test_replay_rejects_each_changed_payload_field(self):
        ledger = Ledger({'a': 10, 'b': 10, 'c': 10})
        original = operation(amount=2, key='one')
        ledger.transfer(**original)
        for field, value in (('source', 'c'), ('target', 'c'), ('amount', 3)):
            with self.subTest(field=field):
                candidate = dict(original, **{field: value})
                self.assert_rejected_without_change(
                    ledger, lambda: ledger.transfer(**candidate)
                )

    def test_new_key_applies_an_equal_payload_again(self):
        ledger = Ledger({'a': 10, 'b': 0})
        ledger.transfer('a', 'b', 2, 'one')
        ledger.transfer('a', 'b', 2, 'two')
        self.assertEqual(ledger.balances, {'a': 6, 'b': 4})
        self.assertEqual(set(ledger.history), {'one', 'two'})

    def test_returned_receipts_cannot_change_history_or_later_replays(self):
        ledger = Ledger({'a': 10, 'b': 0})
        expected = operation(amount=3, key='one')
        receipt = ledger.transfer(**expected)
        receipt.clear()
        replay = ledger.transfer(**expected)
        self.assertEqual(replay, expected)
        replay['amount'] = 999
        replay['key'] = 'changed'
        self.assertEqual(ledger.history, {'one': expected})
        self.assertEqual(ledger.transfer(**expected), expected)
        self.assertEqual(ledger.balances, {'a': 7, 'b': 3})

    def test_failed_transfer_does_not_reserve_key(self):
        ledger = Ledger({'a': 5, 'b': 0})
        self.assert_rejected_without_change(
            ledger, lambda: ledger.transfer('a', 'b', 6, 'retry')
        )
        expected = operation(amount=3, key='retry')
        self.assertEqual(ledger.transfer(**expected), expected)
        self.assertEqual(ledger.balances, {'a': 2, 'b': 3})

    def test_empty_account_name_and_whitespace_key_are_valid(self):
        ledger = Ledger({'': 3, ' b ': 0})
        expected = operation(source='', target=' b ', amount=3, key=' ')
        self.assertEqual(ledger.transfer(**expected), expected)
        self.assertEqual(ledger.balances, {'': 0, ' b ': 3})

    def test_empty_batch_preserves_state(self):
        for ledger in (Ledger({}), Ledger({'a': 10, 'b': 0})):
            if ledger.balances:
                ledger.transfer('a', 'b', 1, 'seed')
            balances, history = ledger.balances, ledger.history
            before = deepcopy((balances, history))
            self.assertEqual(ledger.batch([]), [])
            self.assertEqual((ledger.balances, ledger.history), before)
            self.assertIs(ledger.balances, balances)
            self.assertIs(ledger.history, history)

    def test_batch_requires_list(self):
        ledger = Ledger({'a': 10, 'b': 0})
        for operations in (None, {}, (), 'operations', True, iter([operation()])):
            with self.subTest(operations=operations):
                self.assert_rejected_without_change(
                    ledger, lambda: ledger.batch(operations)
                )

    def test_malformed_batch_operations_roll_back_valid_prefix(self):
        invalid_operations = [None, 1, [], 'operation', {},
                              dict(operation(), extra=1),
                              {**operation(), 1: 'unexpected'}]
        for field in operation():
            missing_field = operation()
            del missing_field[field]
            invalid_operations.append(missing_field)
        invalid_operations.extend([
            operation(amount=True), operation(amount=0), operation(key=[]),
            operation(source=[]), operation(target='missing'), operation(target='a'),
        ])
        for invalid in invalid_operations:
            with self.subTest(invalid=invalid):
                ledger = Ledger({'a': 10, 'b': 0})
                ledger.transfer('a', 'b', 1, 'seed')
                self.assert_rejected_without_change(
                    ledger, lambda: ledger.batch([operation(key='prefix'), invalid])
                )

    def test_failed_batch_at_each_position_preserves_state(self):
        for position in range(3):
            with self.subTest(position=position):
                ledger = Ledger({'a': 10, 'b': 3, 'c': 0})
                ledger.transfer('a', 'c', 1, 'seed')
                operations = [operation(amount=2, key='first'),
                              operation(source='b', target='c', amount=2, key='last')]
                operations.insert(position, operation(amount=100, key='overdraw'))
                before = deepcopy(operations)
                self.assert_rejected_without_change(
                    ledger, lambda: ledger.batch(operations)
                )
                self.assertEqual(operations, before)

    def test_batch_conflicting_replay_rolls_back_for_old_and_new_keys(self):
        for key in ('seed', 'new'):
            with self.subTest(key=key):
                ledger = Ledger({'a': 10, 'b': 0})
                ledger.transfer('a', 'b', 1, 'seed')
                self.assert_rejected_without_change(
                    ledger, lambda: ledger.batch([
                        operation(amount=2), operation(amount=3, key=key)
                    ])
                )

    def test_batch_duplicate_receipts_and_inputs_are_independent(self):
        ledger = Ledger({'a': 5, 'b': 0})
        expected = operation(amount=5)
        operations = [expected.copy(), expected.copy()]
        receipts = ledger.batch(operations)
        self.assertEqual(receipts, [expected, expected])
        self.assertEqual(ledger.balances, {'a': 0, 'b': 5})
        self.assertEqual(ledger.history, {'new': expected})
        receipts[0].clear()
        operations[0]['amount'] = 999
        self.assertEqual(receipts[1], expected)
        self.assertEqual(ledger.history, {'new': expected})
        receipts[1]['source'] = 'changed'
        self.assertEqual(ledger.transfer(**expected), expected)

    def test_integrated_transfer_batch_replay_failure_and_recovery(self):
        ledger = Ledger({'checking': 120, 'savings': 0, 'merchant': 0})
        balances, history = ledger.balances, ledger.history
        seed = operation('checking', 'savings', 20, 'seed')
        self.assertEqual(ledger.transfer(**seed), seed)
        purchase = operation('checking', 'merchant', 70, 'purchase')
        refund = operation('merchant', 'savings', 15, 'refund')
        cashback = operation('savings', 'checking', 5, 'cashback')
        operations = [seed, purchase, refund, purchase, cashback]
        before_operations = deepcopy(operations)
        self.assertEqual(ledger.batch(operations), before_operations)
        self.assertEqual(operations, before_operations)
        self.assertEqual(balances, {'checking': 35, 'savings': 30, 'merchant': 55})
        self.assertEqual(history, {op['key']: op for op in before_operations})
        committed = deepcopy((balances, history))
        self.assertEqual(ledger.batch(operations), before_operations)
        self.assertEqual((balances, history), committed)

        later = operation('checking', 'merchant', 10, 'later')
        overdraft = operation('savings', 'merchant', 31, 'retry')
        self.assert_rejected_without_change(
            ledger, lambda: ledger.batch([later, overdraft])
        )
        recovered = operation('savings', 'merchant', 30, 'retry')
        self.assertEqual(ledger.batch([later, recovered]), [later, recovered])
        self.assertEqual(balances, {'checking': 25, 'savings': 0, 'merchant': 95})
        self.assertEqual(history, {
            **committed[1], 'later': later, 'retry': recovered,
        })
        self.assertEqual(sum(balances.values()), 120)
        self.assertIs(ledger.balances, balances)
        self.assertIs(ledger.history, history)


if __name__ == '__main__':
    unittest.main()
